records.source_meaning: The Barkeep calls Ian byname andtells him tocarry this. Preserve the ordinary work instruction withoutinventing a cargo type or destination yet.
records.fresh_source_gloss: The Barkeep calls Ian byname andtells him tocarry this. Preserve the ordinary work instruction withoutinventing a cargo type or destination yet.
records.whole_exchange_context:
Ian works serving drinks for the Barkeep. A couple comments onhis beauty andquestions whether he is a man;Ian's inner reaction shows thatbeing treated as a spectacle is recurring andunwelcome. The woman is excited byhis serving her andher male companion resents it. A Patron calls Ian a young woman,requests thathe pour a drink,comments onhis appearance/fair skin andquestions his being male. Ian stays silent untilunwanted touching prompts Don't touch me. The Patron cries out inharmed surprise,swears andsarcastically complains abouttreatment ofa customer;Ian realizes he haslost restraint andapologizes formally. Do notinvent a specific wound,grabbing technique,rape threat orpunishment. The later Barkeep explicitly objects tohis use ofa sword,so do noterase the blade reference orassert thatonly a harmless verbal exchange occurred. Lil orders a drink;optional Fernando orders more andEmilio asks forfood. The Barkeep draws Ian aside,says the job doesnot suit him,objects tothe trouble andsword use,andfires him. Ian accepts quietly. Oyaji-san is a familiar address tothis older employer,not evidence ofa father/son relationship.
Lil is intrigued bythe beautiful stranger's melancholy eyes andpossible past. Camille gives curt answers;she teases thathe is jealous andhe stammers a denial. This isexplicit dialogue teasing,not a narrator confirmation ofjealousy or an invented romance. She goes totalk toIan. His inner thoughts reveal unemployment,no money andlonging toreturn tosea afterseeing ships offshore. The earlier Patron finds him alone,calls out again andsummons a group forrevenge afterthe humiliation. Ian judges he cannot defeat themall andtargets onlythe man whoappears tolead them. The Patron scolds his followers;the Retainer leers abouthis pretty face andfinds his fighting enticing. Preserve the sexualized harassment as the aggressor's speech,not mutual attraction or narrator approval. Ian tires andcannot getclose tothe leader alone;the Patron orders his men tofinish him. Lil intervenes,saying she cannot leave such a handsome man introuble. The Patron retreats,claiming he onlyfights battles he canwin andthreatening thathe willremember this. No invented faction,noble/military rank orproof ofactual in-game combat victory.
Afterthe rescue,Lil enthusiastically compliments Ian's looks. Camille makes a source-explicit joke thatFI looks unmistakably like a man nexttoIan;optional Fernando laughs andagrees,andLil protests. Keep it as their rude teasing,not a narrator statement aboutanyone's gender identity. Ian privately dismisses theimportance ofappearance;Lil isoffended because she meant a compliment. He clarifies he was talking tohimself,apologizes andthanks themall forsaving his life. Lil turns thefavor intoa request andIan agrees ifhe canhelp. She explains they aresailors andoffers him work forhis skill as a bodyguard/travel companion. He pauses;Camille politely asks iftheoffer isunacceptable. Ian says he welcomes it. Lil jokingly assumes itis because she isattractive;Camille's aside questions her audacity givenIan's beauty. Ian courteously acknowledges her appeal,thenreveals thathe is an unemployed navigator whose previous ship sank. Preserve the ship he wasaboard,not invented ownership/captaincy. The chance togo tosea again genuinelyhelps him. Lil realizes thearrangement benefits bothsides andasks his name;he introduces himself as Ian Dukov. The spoken acceptance remains distinct froman earned recruitment effect. Source macro counts are {'FI': 2, 'FA': 0, 'FO': 0};branch,presentation,resource,transition andeffect obligations remain separate fromprose.

The woman is excited byhis serving her andher male companion resents it. A Patron calls Ian a young woman,requests thathe pour a drink,comments onhis appearance/fair skin andquestions his being male. Ian stays silent untilunwanted touching prompts Don't touch me. The Patron cries out inharmed surprise,swears andsarcastically complains abouttreatment ofa customer;Ian realizes he haslost restraint andapologizes formally. Do notinvent a specific wound,grabbing technique,rape threat orpunishment. The later Barkeep explicitly objects tohis use ofa sword,so do noterase the blade reference orassert thatonly a harmless verbal exchange occurred. Lil orders a drink;optional Fernando orders more andEmilio asks forfood. The Barkeep draws Ian aside,says the job doesnot suit him,objects tothe trouble andsword use,andfires him. Ian accepts quietly. Oyaji-san is a familiar address tothis older employer,not evidence ofa father/son relationship.
Lil is intrigued bythe beautiful stranger's melancholy eyes andpossible past. Camille gives curt answers;she teases thathe is jealous andhe stammers a denial. This isexplicit dialogue teasing,not a narrator confirmation ofjealousy or an invented romance. She goes totalk toIan. His inner thoughts reveal unemployment,no money andlonging toreturn tosea afterseeing ships offshore. The earlier Patron finds him alone,calls out again andsummons a group forrevenge afterthe humiliation. Ian judges he cannot defeat themall andtargets onlythe man whoappears tolead them. The Patron scolds his followers;the Retainer leers abouthis pretty face andfinds his fighting enticing. Preserve the sexualized harassment as the aggressor's speech,not mutual attraction or narrator approval. Ian tires andcannot getclose tothe leader alone;the Patron orders his men tofinish him. Lil intervenes,saying she cannot leave such a handsome man introuble. The Patron retreats,claiming he onlyfights battles he canwin andthreatening thathe willremember this. No invented faction,noble/military rank orproof ofactual in-game combat victory.
Afterthe rescue,Lil enthusiastically compliments Ian's looks. Camille makes a source-explicit joke thatFI looks unmistakably like a man nexttoIan;optional Fernando laughs andagrees,andLil protests. Keep it as their rude teasing,not a narrator statement aboutanyone's gender identity. Ian privately dismisses theimportance ofappearance;Lil isoffended because she meant a compliment. He clarifies he was talking tohimself,apologizes andthanks themall forsaving his life. Lil turns thefavor intoa request andIan agrees ifhe canhelp. She explains they aresailors andoffers him work forhis skill as a bodyguard/travel companion. He pauses;Camille politely asks iftheoffer isunacceptable. Ian says he welcomes it. Lil jokingly assumes itis because she isattractive;Camille's aside questions her audacity givenIan's beauty. Ian courteously acknowledges her appeal,thenreveals thathe is an unemployed navigator whose previous ship sank. Preserve the ship he wasaboard,not invented ownership/captaincy. The chance togo tosea again genuinelyhelps him. Lil realizes thearrangement benefits bothsides andasks his name;he introduces himself as Ian Dukov. The spoken acceptance remains distinct froman earned recruitment effect. Ian stays silent untilunwanted touching prompts Don't touch me. The Patron cries out inharmed surprise,swears andsarcastically complains abouttreatment ofa customer;Ian realizes he haslost restraint andapologizes formally. Do notinvent a specific wound,grabbing technique,rape threat orpunishment. The later Barkeep explicitly objects tohis use ofa sword,so do noterase the blade reference orassert thatonly a harmless verbal exchange occurred. Lil orders a drink;optional Fernando orders more andEmilio asks forfood. The Barkeep draws Ian aside,says the job doesnot suit him,objects tothe trouble andsword use,andfires him. Ian accepts quietly. Oyaji-san is a familiar address tothis older employer,not evidence ofa father/son relationship.
Lil is intrigued bythe beautiful stranger's melancholy eyes andpossible past. Camille gives curt answers;she teases thathe is jealous andhe stammers a denial. This isexplicit dialogue teasing,not a narrator confirmation ofjealousy or an invented romance. She goes totalk toIan. His inner thoughts reveal unemployment,no money andlonging toreturn tosea afterseeing ships offshore. The earlier Patron finds him alone,calls out again andsummons a group forrevenge afterthe humiliation. Ian judges he cannot defeat themall andtargets onlythe man whoappears tolead them. The Patron scolds his followers;the Retainer leers abouthis pretty face andfinds his fighting enticing. Preserve the sexualized harassment as the aggressor's speech,not mutual attraction or narrator approval. Ian tires andcannot getclose tothe leader alone;the Patron orders his men tofinish him. Lil intervenes,saying she cannot leave such a handsome man introuble. The Patron retreats,claiming he onlyfights battles he canwin andthreatening thathe willremember this. No invented faction,noble/military rank orproof ofactual in-game combat victory.
Afterthe rescue,Lil enthusiastically compliments Ian's looks. Camille makes a source-explicit joke thatFI looks unmistakably like a man nexttoIan;optional Fernando laughs andagrees,andLil protests. Keep it as their rude teasing,not a narrator statement aboutanyone's gender identity. Ian privately dismisses theimportance ofappearance;Lil isoffended because she meant a compliment. He clarifies he was talking tohimself,apologizes andthanks themall forsaving his life. Lil turns thefavor intoa request andIan agrees ifhe canhelp. She explains they aresailors andoffers him work forhis skill as a bodyguard/travel companion. He pauses;Camille politely asks iftheoffer isunacceptable. Ian says he welcomes it. Lil jokingly assumes itis because she isattractive;Camille's aside questions her audacity givenIan's beauty. Ian courteously acknowledges her appeal,thenreveals thathe is an unemployed navigator whose previous ship sank. Preserve the ship he wasaboard,not invented ownership/captaincy. The chance togo tosea again genuinelyhelps him. Lil realizes thearrangement benefits bothsides andasks his name;he introduces himself as Ian Dukov. The spoken acceptance remains distinct froman earned recruitment effect.
